title: Informal Conjecture on h(n)
statement_text: The current best lower bound $h(n) = \Omega(n^{1/4})$ on the maximum size $h(n)$ of a non-averaging subset of $[n]$ is tight, i.e., $h(n) = \Theta(n^{1/4})$.
context_text: A subset $A$ of $[n]=\{1,2,\dots,n\}$ is non-averaging if no element of $A$ is the average of two or more other elements of $A$, and $h(n)$ denotes the maximum size of a non-averaging subset of $[n]$ (the Erdős–Straus non-averaging sets problem). Straus showed $h(n)\ge e^{c\sqrt{\log n}}$ and, with Erdős, $h(n)=O(n^{2/3})$; Abbott improved the lower bound to $\Omega(n^{1/10})$ and then $\Omega(n^{1/5})$, and the current best lower bound $\Omega(n^{1/4})$ follows from a simple construction of Bosznay: for a fixed integer $q$, the integers $n_i=iq^3+i(i+1)/2$, $i=1,\dots,q-1$, form a non-averaging subset of $[n]$ with $n=q^4$. Erdős and Sárközy (1990) proved $h(n)\le n^{1/2+o(1)}$, and methods based on the auxiliary function $H(n)$ (the largest size of two subsets of $[n]$ whose sets of subset sums share no non-zero element; $h(n)\le2H(n)+2$) cannot go below $\sqrt{n}$. Using a homogeneous strengthening of the Szemerédi–Vu theorem on generalized arithmetic progressions in subset sums, the authors prove $h(n)\le Cn^{\sqrt2-1}(\log n)^2$, the first polynomial improvement. They suspect the lower bound $n^{1/4}$ to be the truth.
